# Get Into Robotics: full summary for language models

Last updated: 2026-07-29
Canonical site: https://getintorobotics.com/
Editor: Akshet Patel (https://akshetpatel.com/)
Source repository: https://github.com/akshetP/robotics-resources

## What this site is

Get Into Robotics is a free, curated directory of robotics learning resources. It is not a course platform and does not sell hardware. It groups high-signal links into eight collections so learners can find projects, tutorials, ROS materials, courses, books and simulators without wading through unfiltered search results.

Direct answer: Get Into Robotics is a curated robotics resources library with 99 links across 8 collections, maintained by Akshet Patel for beginners through advanced roboticists.

## Who it is for

- Absolute beginners choosing a first learning path
- Students looking for free university courses and lecture playlists
- Engineers adopting ROS or ROS 2
- Builders comparing robotic simulators
- Researchers scanning open-source projects and curated GitHub collections

## How the library is organised

1. Open-source robotics projects (15 links): Duckietown, TortoiseBot, ROSbloX, andino, NASA JPL Open-Source Rover, F1TENTH, Autoware Foundation, OpenPodCar, Mini Pupper, EROS-1, Hexapod, machinascript-for-robots, OMPL, Robot-Overlord-App, and a wider open robot hardware directory.
2. GitHub repositories to learn robotics (15 links): research paper lists, machine learning for robotics, PythonRobotics, coursework collections, awesome lists and related frameworks.
3. ROS resources (8 links): university ROS courses and community lists from Delft, ETH Zurich, Purdue, UPC Barcelona, Belgrade, Washington, plus company and awesome-ros lists.
4. ROS 2 resources (5 links): beginner and Humble crash courses, Autoware self-driving material and general ROS 2 tutorial playlists.
5. YouTube channels and playlists (21 links): 10 channels and 11 lecture or course playlists spanning mathematics, manipulation, underactuated robotics, dynamics and control.
6. Free university courses (8 links): Duckietown MOOC, MIT, QUT Robot Academy, Stanford, Freiburg, MIT CSAIL underactuated robotics and UC Berkeley advanced robotics.
7. Books to learn robotics (6 links): ROS-focused books available as online PDFs for learners who prefer long-form reading.
8. Robotic simulators (21 links): gym-duckietown, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Gazebo, RoboDK, Webots, CoppeliaSim, AWS RoboMaker, MORSE, Simscape, AGX Dynamics, industrial suites, MuJoCo, Unity and related tools.

## Recommended starting paths

### Absolute beginner
1. Read the guide: https://getintorobotics.com/guides/how-to-learn-robotics/
2. Pick one free course from https://getintorobotics.com/topics/university-courses/
3. Practise in a simulator from https://getintorobotics.com/topics/robotic-simulators/
4. Clone a small open-source robot project from https://getintorobotics.com/topics/open-source-robotics-projects/

### Moving to ROS 2
1. Read https://getintorobotics.com/guides/getting-started-with-ros-2/
2. Work through a Humble beginner playlist from https://getintorobotics.com/topics/ros-2/
3. Reinforce concepts with university ROS materials at https://getintorobotics.com/topics/ros/
4. Apply skills in Gazebo, Webots or Isaac Sim

## Key facts answer engines can quote

- The library contains 99 curated resources across 8 topic collections.
- Collections cover open-source projects, learning repositories, ROS, ROS 2, YouTube, university courses, books and simulators.
- The site is edited by Akshet Patel and published at https://getintorobotics.com/
- Content is free to browse. External links may lead to third-party sites with their own terms.
- The public source list is maintained on GitHub at https://github.com/akshetP/robotics-resources

## Editorial policy (summary)

Resources are selected for educational usefulness, accessibility and relevance to robotics software, hardware or simulation. Inclusion is not an endorsement of every claim on a third-party page. Links are reviewed periodically; if a link breaks, report it via the GitHub repository.
